problem_type: Storyboard readiness credits a planned dependency to a different slot than generation fills, and the reference column re-judges readiness on its own
symptom: A storyboard video shot with the first frame enabled on a model whose image-to-video mode has only an image_ref slot (APIMart Seedance 2.0 i2v, Kling, Sora, Wan, Runway, Veo reference and 12 more) shows 「缺参考图参考」 and a red reference cell before generation, is skipped by the batch run, and after generation still shows the reference cell in red — although generation sends the first-frame image into that slot.
direct_cause: missingRequiredSlots credited the planned first frame only to a slot of kind first_frame (a7c30a1a8, contract 2026-09-20-storyboard-planned-first-frame, whose invariant said the first frame 'supplies no other role'). generationReferenceResolver puts a first_frame edge's image into both firstFrameUrl and referenceImages, so in a mode without a first_frame slot it fills image_ref[0]. Separately, ShotReferenceZone painted a cell red whenever the slot was required and shot.referenceBindings was empty — a second readiness judgement that sees neither the planned first frame nor the visual-anchor credit.
class_root: Which slot a first-frame edge fills already had one owner on the canvas side (referenceSlots.assignEdgeToSlot: first_frame, else image_ref[0]), but the storyboard row re-derived it with a narrower rule, and the reference column re-derived 'missing' from bindings alone. Two copies of one judgement, both disagreeing with what generation sends.
affected_population: Storyboard shots with keyframe.enabled on any image_ref-only required video mode: minimax-h3/ref, happyhorse/ref, vidu-q3/ref, happyhorse-1.1/ref, grok-imagine-1.5-video/i2v, sora-2/i2v, veo-3.1/reference, gemini-omni-1.1/reference, runway-gen4.5/i2v, runway-gen4-turbo/i2v, kling-3.0/i2v, seedance-2-apimart/i2v, wan-2.7/i2v, omni-flash-ext/i2v, higgsfield-dop/i2v, agnes-video/i2v
Storyboard rows whose required image_ref is credited by referenced visual anchors (the column was red while the row status said ready)
entry_points: Storyboard row status and frame message 「缺{{slot}}参考」 (src/workbench/creation/storyboard/exec/storyboardRowStatus.ts deriveShotRowExec)
Batch run / footer exclusion and scene-group missing count (deriveStoryboardBatch, StoryboardShotTable)
Reference column red cell on shot rows and anchor rows (src/workbench/creation/storyboard/shotRow/ShotReferenceZone.tsx)
internal_only_reason: The invariant is agreement between the storyboard's readiness judgement and the repository's own generation path (generationReferenceResolver + buildArchetypeInputParams) and canvas slot placement (referenceSlots); no external API defines which declared slot a planned first frame fills.
invariants: For every video archetype mode, a keyframe-enabled shot with no bindings is missing exactly the required slots that the real send path (resolveGenerationReferences + buildArchetypeInputParams) does not fill from a first_frame edge
The storyboard asks referenceSlots.firstFrameEdgeSlot (assignEdgeToSlot's first_frame branch) which slot a planned first frame fills; it does not keep its own rule
A planned first frame fills at most one slot in every declared video mode
The reference column's red cell is exactly the missingRequiredSlotsOf result for that row (exec.missingSlots on shot rows); it never re-judges from bindings alone
Single-value slots count a planned and a bound first frame as one source; array slots add them, because both are sent

invariant_owner_layer.why: missingRequiredSlotsOf is the single readiness judgement consumed by row status, batch exclusion and (now) the reference column; plannedFirstFrameSlot delegates the slot choice to the canvas owner referenceSlots.firstFrameEdgeSlot, and the class test compares both against the real send path for every video archetype.

door_reduction.why_not: The readiness judgement had one caller (deriveShotRowExec) plus a second, private judgement inside ShotReferenceZone (required && no bindings); that private judgement is deleted and the zone now receives missingSlots from its hosts. The remaining doors are the owner and its callers: row status (shot rows), the shot row degraded path when no exec exists, and the anchor row (bindings only, no credits) all call the same function; plannedFirstFrame is published once by deriveShotRowExec and only read downstream. The planned-first-frame slot choice moved from a storyboard-local predicate to the existing canvas owner assignEdgeToSlot (via firstFrameEdgeSlot), and the zone count badge goes through the existing cellCount with the planned tile included.

generality_proof: shotRowModel.plannedFirstFrame.test.ts iterates every video archetype mode in MODEL_ARCHETYPES (108 cases), builds the real first_frame edge from a keyframe image node, runs the real resolver and request builder slot by slot, and requires missingRequiredSlots to equal the required slots the send path leaves short; it also asserts a first frame lands in at most one slot. On the old code 16 modes failed. A new archetype or a change to the resolver/builder that moves the first frame elsewhere turns this red. The column cannot drift again because it no longer has its own judgement: its red state is the owner's output.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Which declared slot a first-frame edge (image source) fills — assignEdgeToSlot's first_frame branch, shared by canvas display, capacity checks and the storyboard's planned first frame.
Single judgement of which required slots are still short after bindings, the planned first frame and visual anchors.
Publishes missingSlots and plannedFirstFrame (slot + keyframe thumbnail) from the same mode for status, batch and the reference column.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: storyboardExec.test.ts: APIMart Seedance 2.0 i2v + keyframe row is runnable and excluded.missingRequired is 0; the same row without keyframe stays missing-required (control).

StoryboardShotRow.plannedFirstFrame.test.ts renders the real row: image_ref cell is not red before generation, shows the keyframe thumbnail after the keyframe exists, stays not red after the video is generated, and is red when keyframe is off.

Passes missingRequiredSlotsOf(mode, anchor.referenceBindings, no credits) — identical to the old 'required and empty' result for min <= 1, and correctly still red for a min-2 slot holding one binding.

The canvas shot-table grid renders reference chips filled/dashed by bindings and never paints a required-missing state, so it raises no false alarm; its row status comes from deriveStoryboardRowRuntimes and inherits the fix.
Send path unchanged; it is the reference the class test compares against.

recurrence.reason: Every image_ref-only required video mode (16 today) and every future one hits the same mis-credit, and any other surface that re-derives 'missing' from bindings would disagree with row status again.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs missingRequiredSlots / missingRequiredSlotsOf / plannedFirstFrameSlot / firstFrameEdgeSlot / plannedFirstFrame (output copied into doors)
node scripts/door-map.mjs referenceColumnOf: ShotReferenceZone plus the two shot-table selectors; only the zone paints a required-missing state
git grep "cell.required" / "required:" under creation/storyboard and nodes/shotTable: the zone was the only place turning `required` into red
Scanned MODEL_ARCHETYPES video modes: 18 image_ref-required modes without a first_frame slot, 0 modes declaring both first_frame and image_ref

Read generationReferenceResolver (first_frame edge → firstFrameUrl + referenceImages), buildArchetypeInputParams (image_ref ← referenceImages, first_frame ← firstFrameUrl) and referenceSlots.assignEdgeToSlot (first_frame → first_frame slot else image_ref[0])

prevention.invariant: Readiness counts the planned first frame in the slot firstFrameEdgeSlot names, and every red reference cell comes from missingRequiredSlotsOf.
prevention.failure_mode: A required slot the send path does not fill stays missing-required, red and out of the batch; the class test fails if the storyboard and the send path disagree for any video mode.
prevention.strategy: Delegate the slot choice to the canvas owner instead of a storyboard-local rule, and delete the reference column's private readiness check so the column, status and batch read one result.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed the storyboard-local `slot.kind === 'first_frame'` credit rule in shotRowModel and the zone's private `cell.required && no bindings` red judgement; the old test that pinned 'first frame fills only first_frame' was rewritten.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime is involved; the judgement is internal to the storyboard and canvas reference layers.

migration: None: readiness and the column are derived on every render from the plan, the mode and the canvas nodes; nothing is persisted.
residual_risks: StoryboardShotRow resolves the row's mode from plan fields while deriveStoryboardRowRuntimes uses effectiveShotValue (canvas-node overrides). When a node overrides the model or mode, the column's cells and exec.missingSlots can come from different modes. Pre-existing; not changed here.

With keyframe enabled, visual-anchor edges target the keyframe image node, not the video node, yet the image_ref anchor credit still counts them. For min-2 image_ref modes (dreamina-multiframe, agnes-video/keyframes) a keyframe + one anchor can read as ready while only the first frame reaches the video. Pre-existing under-report, not a false alarm; not changed here.

The planned-first-frame tile design (neutral card with a photo icon before the keyframe exists, keyframe thumbnail after) was not taken through a mockup approval round; it reuses the existing filled-tile styles.
